newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-LEAFS DEAL MULLER, MURPHY AMONG 18 DEADLINE TRADES.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-LEAFS DEAL MULLER, MURPHY AMONG 18 DEADLINE TRADES.

text.p: The Toronto Maple Leafs continued cost-cutting and rebuilding Tuesday, unloading veterans Kirk Muller and Larry Murphy amid a flurry of activity around the National Hockey League prior to its afternoon trading deadline.
There were no blockbuster deals or superstars switching uniforms Tuesday, but a total of 18 trades involving 35 players were completed before the 3:00 p.m. (1900 GMT) deadline, according to the NHL.

The Leafs, who sent popular captain Doug Gilmour to New Jersey late last month, traded Muller to the Florida Panthers for 21-year-old forward Jason Podollan, and shipped defenceman Larry Murphy and his big contract to Detroit.
The Red Wings, who were looking for a defensive-minded blueliner, did not have to part with any manpower to get the league's third highest-scoring defenceman ever.

Toronto has now dumped three of its top five salaries, and with the team mired in 12th place in the Western Conference at 26-38-6, General Manager Cliff Fletcher has written off the current season. "As far as we're concerned, this is the start of the 1997-98 season for us tomorrow," he said.
Muller, who has been captain of both the New Jersey Devils and Montreal Canadiens in his 13-year NHL career, was pleased with his new address.
"I'm really excited about going to Florida. It gives me a chance to go for the Cup," said the 31-year-old Muller, who helped Montreal win the Stanley Cup in 1993.
Muller has compiled 325 goals and 519 assists in 952 NHL games but was a minus-22 on the ice for Toronto this season.

Murphy had seven goals and 32 assists in 69 games for Toronto, managing a plus-2 rating on one of the league's worst teams. In 1,303 career game, Murphy has 252 goals and 793 assists for 1,045 points, trailing only Paul Coffey and Ray Bourque among defenceman on the all-time scoring list.
Calgary and Edmonton also engaged in some budget trimming, with the Flames sending centre Robert Reichel to the New York Islanders and the Oilers dealing veteran defenceman Jeff Norton to Tampa Bay.

Calgary unloaded Reichel's $2 million salary in exchange for left-winger Marty McInnis, who has just one point less than Reichel this season at nearly a quarter the price ($550,000). The Flames also got a junior goaltender and a sixth-round draft pick.
Reichel, who has just 16 goals and 27 assists, was the second-highest paid player on the Flames roster.
The Oilers picked up 22-year-old defenceman Drew Bannister and his modest $350,000 salary in exchange for Norton, 31, who will make $1.25 million this season.
The Oilers youth movement continued with the acquisition 20-year-old defenceman Craig Millar and 21-year-old left wing Barrie Moore from Buffalo in exchange for Czech left wing Miroslav Satan.
After getting Reichel, the Islanders sent left wing Derek King, their second-leading scorer who had been with the team since 1986, to Hartford for a fifth-round draft pick.
King, 30, who had been with the Islanders longer than any other current player, has 23 goals and 30 assists in 70 games.

In other notable deadline deals, the Los Angeles Kings sent veteran centre Eddie Olczyk to the Pittsburgh Penguins for big right wing Glen Murray, 24, who has yet to live up to expectations in 283 NHL games with Boston and Pittsburgh.
Olczyk, who signed with the Kings as a free agent in July, has 21 goals and 23 assists in 67 games. The 31-year-old centre has 315 goals and 419 assists in 869 career games.
The Pens also picked up right wing Roman Oksiuta from the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim for Korean-born centre Richard Park.
The Canadiens and Phoenix Coyotes also did some deadline dealing.
The Coyotes, who have started goaltender Nikolai Khabibulin in 31 straight games, acquired 29-year-old backup Pat Jablonski for 21-year-old defenceman Steve Cheredaryk.

Montreal also acquired rugged defenceman Dave Manson from Phoenix in exchange for defenceman Murray Baron and tough guy Chris Murray. Phoenix then sent Murray to Hartford for veteran defenceman Gerald Diduck.
